definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese festival day marking seasonal transitions, originally derived from Chinese calendar customs. There are five major seasonal festivals throughout the year.

examples.japanese: {五月|ごがつ}の{節句|せっく}を{祝|いわ}う。
examples.english: To celebrate the May seasonal festival.

examples.japanese: {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}に{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: We display hina dolls for the Peach Festival.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{五|いつ}つの{節句|せっく}があり、それぞれに{特別|とくべつ}な{料理|りょうり}や{飾|かざ}りがある。
examples.english: There are five seasonal festivals in Japan, each with its own special foods and decorations.

notes:
Originally from Chinese customs marking seasonal turning points. The five major {節句|せっく} ({五節句|ごせっく}) are:
- {人日|じんじつ} (January 7) — Seven Herb Festival
- {上巳|じょうし} (March 3) — {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく} (Girls' Day / Doll Festival)
- {端午|たんご} (May 5) — {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day / Children's Day)
- {七夕|たなばた} (July 7) — Star Festival
- {重陽|ちょうよう} (September 9) — Chrysanthemum Festival

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}: Peach Festival (Girls' Day, March 3)
- {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}: Boys' Day (May 5)
- {五節句|ごせっく}: the five seasonal festivals
- {節句|せっく}{料理|りょうり}: seasonal festival food
- {節句|せっく}{飾|かざ}り: seasonal festival decorations

CULTURAL NOTE:
The March and May festivals remain widely celebrated in modern Japan. Families with daughters display {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう} (hina dolls) in March, and families with sons display {鎧兜|よろいかぶと} (armor and helmets) or {鯉|こい}のぼり (carp streamers) in May.
